programmes.d: Philip Serrell spends big on a butter churn. Catherine Southon finds two 1940s compacts.

TV presenters Fiona Phillips and Richard Madeley go head-to-head with the help of experts Charles Hanson and James Braxton, in search of antique treasures. They travel the entire length of Cornwall, from Lostwithiel to auction in Bude.
Catherine Southon and Tim Medhurst visit Worcestershire, Oxfordshire and Gloucestershire. Tim unearths what could be a Roman coffin and Catherine phones a friend.
Catherine Southon buys a croquet set. Phil Serrell learns the etymology of "airport."
A girl with some cherries lures Tim Medhurst to part with his cash, while Catherine Southon looks to a kaleidoscope for profit. Who'll reign in Wilshire and claim this Road Trip?

Dancers and rivals, Arlene Phillips and Anton du Beke compete with the help of experts James Braxton and Charles Hanson, touring West Yorkshire, a traditional clog-making business and wonderful Blackpool Tower before ending up in Liverpool.
Catherine Southon decides to change her strategy. Phil Serrell talks to a local fisherman.
Veteran Road Tripper James Braxton tours the southeast with novice Izzie Balmer, an auctioneer with a penchant for jewelry. Will she take the crown with her jewels?
Catherine Southon sees cables that stretch across the ocean. Phil Serrell goes for a ride.

Old friends Michael Aspel and Una Stubbs hit the road with their antiques experts, Thomas Plant and James Lewis. They're hunting for the best antique deals, traveling through the delightful county of Norfolk, to an auction in King's Lynn.
Izzie Balmer goes on a mission to Bletchley Park where codebreakers cracked messages from Hitler, while James Braxton dons a bandana and takes on English badminton.
Catherine Southon heads to the Royal Mint and Phil Serrell gets a lesson in culture.

Actors Alison Steadman and Larry Lamb add drama to the hunt for profits, as they team up with antiques experts Thomas Plant and Paul Laidlaw. Their trip begins in Arundel, then cruises along the Sussex coast to an auction at Eastbourne.
It’s all rosy for Paul Laidlaw and Claire Rawle. Then Claire reveals she loves militaria!
Izzie Balmer tries out a winter sport that began in the Fens. James is fuelled by the food of the common man. And they're buying chairs like they're going out of fashion for a Suffolk auction.

Jon Culshaw and Debra Stephenson team up with experts Thomas Plant and Mark Stacey, hunting antique bargains in and around Edinburgh before auction in Essex. Who will win the day? Hopefully both teams, as all profits go to Children in Need.
It's a Volunteer Life Brigade and military post for Paul Laidlaw and Claire Rawle.

Izzie Balmer and James Braxton visit the most easterly point. Izzie just can't resist the attractions of chairs -- Edwardian and Georgian. And James can't say no to a gigantic wine rack to go with his French cafe table.
Claire Rawle talks big game fishing in 1930s. Paul Laidlaw sets off for a WWII bunker.

Eastenders veterans Pam St Clement and Rudolph Walker team up with experts Charles Hanson and James Braxton. They seek out antiques from East Sussex, Tumbridge, Wells in Kent, and finish up--dramatically--at auction at Rayleigh in Essex.
Izzie Balmer is waylaid by the taste of Derbyshire and James Braxton takes a punt on some old headlines. It's full steam ahead to the finishing line at Lincoln. Can the tortoise outrun the hare?
Paul Laidlaw finds a rare puzzle jug. Claire Rawle bets on some Shelley porcelain.
A new Trip sees experts Roo Irvine and Angus Ashworth searching for antiques in Northern Ireland. Expect silver jewelry and Victorian furniture made from an unlikely material.

Goalkeepers Peter Shilton and Peter Schmeichel buy and sell antiques around Cheshire, aided by Paul Laidlaw and Mark Stacey. They visit a Cycling Museum in Warrington and a Football Museum in Manchester, ending up at auction in Runcorn.
Paul Laidlaw buys a 17th-century halberd head. Claire Rawle buys an Edwardian inkstand.
Roo Irvine and Angus Ashworth traverse southwest Wales in style, on land and on water. Angus buys cheap, while Roo buys big.
Christina Trevanion talks seaside history. Mark Stacey sees the last Victorian brickworks.

Silent Witness stars Emilia Fox and Tom Ward, aided by experts James Braxton and Charlie Ross, embark on a hunt for antiques to turn a profit. From Glasgow to the Village of Kilbarchan, they end at auction in Billingshurst in West Sussex.
Experts Roo Irvine and Angus Ashworth continue to scour the shops of south Wales for antiques. There are Welsh breakfasts, high-speed boats, and a little panic buying.
In the Cotswolds, Mark Stacey finds a rural idyll and Christina Trevanion unearths a hero.

Masterchef's Gregg Wallace and John Torode feel the heat as they team up with experts Charles Hanson and Charlie Ross. They visit stately homes on their way from Alton in Hampshire to auction at Fernhurst on the Surrey/West Sussex border.
Christina Trevanion ends up deep underground and Mark Stacey has to call for help!
Experts Arusha "Roo" Irvine and Angus Ashworth hit the shops of the west country looking for treasure. But do the bidders in Exmouth like what they've bought?

Sue Holderness and John Challis bargain hunt with Charles Hanson and Philip Serrell in Essex for auction in Kent. Can John outsmart his TV wife or will Sue win big? Hopefully, both teams will do well as all profits go to Children in Need.
Mark Stacey studies death-obsessed Victorians. Christina Trevanion looks into Land Rovers.
It's last time out for experts Arusha "Roo" Irvine and Angus Ashworth, shopping in the west country for their final auction. Roo enjoys the fun of the fair while Angus enjoys a tipple.
Mark Stacey is literally waist deep in antiques. Christina Trevanion buys a unique home.

Heavyweights Germaine Greer and Clive Anderson hit the shops of Lancashire with Charlie Ross and Charles Hanson looking for antiques to auction in Northwich. With trips to Chetham Library and Helmsmore Mill Museum, who will win the day?
Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell start a Road Trip from Cockermouth, though there are doubts they'll make it to the Kendal auction when their classic car breaks down.
Paul Laidlaw finds Cold War stamps. Natasha Raskin gets to grips with an ancient sport.

Stage and screen stars Stefanie Powers and Don Warrington join Charles Hanson and Margie Cooper to make big profits buying and selling antiques. They go from Hertfordshire to auction in West Sussex, with magic and Mosquitos along the way.
Stephanie Connell has a surprise in store for birthday boy Philip Serrell as they cross Caledonia on the second leg of their Trip. Expect gold panning and a novel buy in a book shop.
Natasha Raskin visits a cake factory. Paul Laidlaw sees a side to Cumbria’s wartime past.
Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell are cruising Caledonia in pursuit of profit. Phil eats a square sausage while Steph becomes puppet master. Who'll triumph at the auction in Hamilton?
It's day one of the new series! Anita Manning and Mark Stacey start their journey in Aberfeldy and head for auction glory in Dundee.
Paul Laidlaw can't find anything he likes. Natasha Raskin’s eyes are turned by spindles.
It's still anyone's game, as Anita Manning and Mark Stacey travel from Wiston in South Lanarkshire to Edinburgh.
Phil Serrell and Steph Connell return to Scotland. While all roads point to Dunfermline for auction, Phil sets sail and Steph buys a paddle.
Paul Laidlaw finds a rare boat on the Norfolk Broads. Natasha Raskin looks for bunnies.
Day three of Anita Manning and Mark Stacey's antique hunt takes them from the Scottish borders to Sunderland, with a remarkable find along the way.
Paul Laidlaw and Natasha Raskin dig up an art nouveau food warmer and a table croquet set.
It's experts Stephanie Connell and Philip Serrell's final outing in their classic car and they're in the northeast of England looking for winning wares. The deciding auction is in Darlington.
Day four of Anita Manning and Mark Stacey's journey from St. Helen Auckland to Darlington is derailed when their car breaks down.
James Braxton and Raj Bisram bet on nautical fare for an auction on the Isle of Wight.
In their first Road Trip together, experts Catherine Southon and James Braxton compete for auction glory as they browse, barter and banter across the Home Counties in a 1969 Rover.
Anita Manning and Mark Stacey's final leg takes them from Richmond in North Yorkshire to the auction showdown in Huby near York.
Raj Bisram falls for a teddy and a ride on doggy. Is James Braxton talking to Elton John?
Experts Catherine Southon and James Braxton's antiques adventure takes them through Worcestershire, Warwickshire and the West Midlands. Can James make a profit to catch Catherine?
A new day and a new team: experts Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon start their trip in Aboyne and finish up at an auction in Dundee.
James Braxton has Staffordshire figures to auction. Raj Bisram bets on a Moorcroft vase.
A few pounds separate rival antiquers Catherine Southon and James Braxton. Tactics come into play ahead of a South Yorkshire auction. But there's time to savor a local delicacy.
Day two sees some tactical shenanigans from rivals Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon, as they travel from Perth to Paisley.
James Braxton dives into buying, but all bets are off when Raj Bisram catches up with him.

Catherine Southon and James Braxton's take their antiques hunt to Derbyshire and Leicestershire. How do Catherine's 18th-century caryatid carvings measure up against James's very old bowl full of marbles?
Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon's affections start to wane as they hit the road for day three, crossing the border from Glenluce to Carlisle.
Seven pounds separates James Braxton and Raj Bisram, but there’s still time for detours!
The competition between Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon intensifies as they journey from Sedburgh to Leeds.

With just six pounds separating them, Catherine Southon and James Braxton battle it out on the final leg of their adventure. Will a jug in the shape of an owl or a biscuit tin in the form of a travelling trunk make the biggest profit?
Ann Widdecombe and Craig Revel Horwood hunt with Mark Stacey and Catherine Southon’s help.
Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon head from Skipton to Liverpool for their final auction showdown.

Charlie Ross and Izzie Balmer start their hunt in the bucolic Cotswolds. Charlie picks up a military first aid kit for a quite intimate area. And Izzie's eclectic mix of buys include a toast rack and a tutti-frutti bowl.
Deborah Meaden and Theo Paphitis go head-to-head, aided by Mark Stacey and Thomas Plant.
It's day one for expert Thomas Plant and Road Trip newbie, Scottish auctioneer Paul Laidlaw, as they travel from Skipton to Sheffield.

Charlie Ross and Izzie Balmer continue their trip in Surrey. Izzie finds a piece of jewelry that causes a stir at auction. And Charlie's passion for furniture uncovers a very rare table that sparks a frenzy of bids at the Dorking auction.
Kirsty Wark and Alastair Stewart treasure hunt with Philip Serrell and Catherine Southon.
Day two for dynamic duo Thomas Plant and Paul Laidlaw sees them attempt to outwit each other on their way from Bolsover to the auction in Stamford.

In North Wessex Downs, Charlie Ross hunts for 'sparkly' antiques but is distracted by an Edwardian box that holds a surprise. And Izzie Balmer rummages in a shop's storeroom -- what goodies will she uncover?
